IR.rationale: A rising 5-year yield relative to the funds rate signals hawkish repricing of the expected policy path. That state dominates intermediate and aggregate bond returns, and bond momentum or partial reversal carries it forward.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads together with weak high-yield returns mark credit stress. That typically brings flight-to-quality demand for Treasuries and lower risk-free yields.

V.rationale: High equity implied volatility proxies for risk aversion, which supports safe-haven bond demand. It also lowers expected policy rates.

AP.rationale: Since the late 1990s stock-bond correlation has been negative, so weak equity returns go with falling yields and portfolio rebalancing into Treasuries.

ST.rationale: Cross-sectional equity style factors have no clear mechanism linking them to government bond returns.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation is a classic risk-off and carry-unwind signal that coincides with safe-haven flows into Treasuries.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices push up inflation expectations and nominal yields, which hurts nominal bond returns. The effect is partly offset for inflation-linked bonds.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens with falling jobless claims describe reflationary growth news. That raises expected short rates and term premia, so yields go up.

ENDG.rationale: Bond returns show time-series momentum at multi-week horizons and some short-horizon reversal. Their own recent return is therefore informative, and the model learns the sign.

IR.rationale: Sharp upward repricing of near-term policy relative to the funds rate signals monetary policy uncertainty. Such policy surprises tend to cluster and raise subsequent rate volatility.

B.rationale: Widening credit spreads signal deteriorating conditions in which flight-to-quality flows and liquidity shifts make bond prices more volatile.

V.rationale: High implied equity volatility combined with high policy uncertainty captures an uncertainty regime in which interest-rate volatility is also elevated. Cross-asset volatility comoves.

AP.rationale: Equity sell-offs raise uncertainty through the leverage effect and trigger large rebalancing and safe-haven flows into bonds.

ST.rationale: Equity style factors carry little information about future bond variance beyond the other groups.

FX.rationale: Yen strength signals carry unwinds and global deleveraging episodes, which increase volatility in safe-asset markets.

COM.rationale: Commodity slumps raise uncertainty about inflation and global growth, and so about the policy path and breakevens. This adds to rate volatility.

MC.rationale: High financial stress indicates impaired liquidity and risk-off dynamics that raise bond market volatility beyond its own recent level.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility clustering means recent high realised variance persists. Deviations from the baseline also tend to mean-revert, so own variance remains informative.

IR.rationale: A rising 5-year spread over the funds rate together with curve steepening describes a bear-steepening sell-off driven by term premia. Such sell-offs tend to extend and produce tail losses, especially for long bonds.

B.rationale: Tightening spreads with strong high-yield returns mark risk-on conditions in which safe-haven demand drains out of Treasuries.

V.rationale: Low risk aversion removes the flight-to-quality bid. It leaves duration exposed to growth and inflation repricing.

AP.rationale: Strong equity rallies under negative stock-bond correlation coincide with rising yields and rotation out of bonds.

ST.rationale: Style factors have no clear link to tail losses in government bonds.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength against the yen accompanies rising US yields and risk-on carry positioning, consistent with bond sell-offs.

COM.rationale: Commodity price surges raise inflation expectations and the risk of a hawkish policy response, which fattens the left tail of nominal bond returns.

MC.rationale: Rising breakevens with strengthening labour data describe reflation that can trigger abrupt upward repricing of yields.

ENDG.rationale: Recent weak returns signal an ongoing sell-off. Momentum and convexity-hedging flows make further large losses more likely.

IR.rationale: Falling 1- and 5-year yields relative to the funds rate signal dovish repricing, with markets pricing easing. That state precedes strong duration rallies.

B.rationale: Credit stress drives flight-to-quality demand that can produce outsized Treasury gains.

V.rationale: High market and policy uncertainty together characterise risk-off regimes in which safe-haven bonds rally strongly.

AP.rationale: Broad weakness in US and emerging-market equities signals a global risk-off and growth scare, which favours large bond gains.

ST.rationale: Style factors have no clear link to tail gains in government bonds.

FX.rationale: Yen appreciation reflects safe-haven flows and carry unwinds that coincide with falling US yields.

COM.rationale: Oil price slumps lower inflation expectations and signal weaker growth, which supports large rallies in nominal bonds.

MC.rationale: Rising financial stress with deteriorating labour data describes a growth scare that raises expectations of policy easing, producing outsized bond gains.

ENDG.rationale: Recent strong returns indicate an ongoing rally. Bond time-series momentum makes further large gains more likely.
